paragraphs: In a World Bank Funded APCBTM - Andhra Pradesh Community Based Tank Management Project, ALERT was instrumental in supporting farmers of dry land areas of Krishna district in strengthening minor irrigation tanks for improving Agriculture Production, Food, Nutritional security and Improved living conditions of 3,452 farmers of dry lands to raise one or two food crops through critical irrigation, which contributed to Food security and economic advancement of small farmers.

child-interventions.title: Child Interventions
paragraphs: Awareness & Education: Organized meetings and sensitization programmes for parents and community leaders on child rights and protection laws. Conducted campaigns in villages and schools on sickle cell anemia and documented vital medical data. Developed and distributed child-friendly materials on child rights in local languages.

Protection Mechanisms: Strengthened Child Protection Committees (CPCs) at the village level for identifying and addressing child rights violations with measurable results. Working with law enforcement agencies to ensure effective investigation and prosecution of child rights violations, follow-up on POCSO cases, and comprehensive victim relief measures.

Support Services: Provided access to quality education to Koya tribal children and promoted nutrition gardens in R&R colonies. Undertook targeted healthcare initiatives for children in partnership with Vitamin Angels, alongside recreational sports and community events.

Community Engagement: Mobilized community members into child protection groups, promoted positive parenting practices nurturing childhood, and engaged tribal elders and influencers to promote child rights messages within adivasi communities.

Considering Scheduled Areas: Supported tribal communities to develop culturally appropriate child protection strategies addressing malnutrition, lack of access to education, child abuse, and child labor in culturally sensitive ways.

Monitoring & Media Tracking: ALERT, in partnership with Adivasi Mahasaba, regularly monitors media-reported and formally reported cases of violence against women, children, and Adivasis, following up on rights violations.

Koya Basha & Culture: For over three years, ALERT in partnership with LITDS supports Koya Basha promotion, supporting 5 dedicated teachers orienting Koya and Gothi Koya children on arts, paintings, and cultural festivals.

Solar Hamlets & Resilient Livelihoods: Installed community security solar lights in remote Koya, Gothi Koya, and Konda Reddi villages, besides supplying solar lanterns. Introduced localized adaptation and resilience through FPOs in forestry, horticulture, fisheries, avenue plantation, and agro-tourism across ASR and Eluru districts.

cases.title: Court Cases & Legal Compliances (LA & RR)
cases.subtitle: Official High Court writ petitions, Special LA & R&R Authority dispute references, RTI disclosures, and R&R Commissioner proceedings.
paragraphs: Displacement and compensation disputes under the Polavaram Irrigation Project are adjudicated under the statutory framework of the Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013 (RFCTLARR Act 2013), read with the Andhra Pradesh Land Acquisition Rules. Project-affected families (PAFs) and tribal communities in West Godavari and East Godavari agency tracts have pursued judicial remedies across multiple forums, including the Hon'ble High Court of Andhra Pradesh, the Special Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation & Resettlement Authority (LA & RR Court), and the Office of the Rehabilitation & Resettlement Commissioner.

Under Section 64 of the Act, any project-displaced or land-owning person interested who has not accepted the award may require the Land Acquisition Collector to refer the matter to the Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Authority for judicial determination regarding measurement of land, amount of compensation, apportionment, or statutory rehabilitation entitlements. Official RTI data compiled from 2017 to 2022 documents extensive litigation over valuation discrepancies, exclusion of tribal youth reaching majority from independent family packages, non-implementation of land-for-land allotments under the Second Schedule, and prolonged disbursement delays.

Writ petitions filed before the Hon'ble High Court of Andhra Pradesh for West Godavari (Eluru) and East Godavari (ASR / Rampachodavaram) districts invoke Constitutional guarantees under Article 21 (Right to Life and Livelihood), Article 300A (Right to Property), and Schedule V protective enactments including the Agency Tracts Interest and Land Transfer Act (LTR 1/70) and PESA Act 1996. These proceedings seek judicial enforcement of mandatory R&R colony infrastructure under Schedule III, judicial compliance before reservoir impoundment, and restitution for unnotified submergence tracts.

land-acquisition-la.title: Land Acquisition (LA)
paragraphs: Under the Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement (RFCTLARR) Act 2013, land acquisition in Scheduled and Tribal Agency areas requires mandatory compliance with PESA Gram Sabha consent, Social Impact Assessments (SIA), and strict non-alienation provisions under LTR 1/70.

The acquisition workflow encompasses Section 11 preliminary notification, Section 15 hearing of objections, Section 19 declaration of acquisition, and Section 23 award inquiries by Special Land Acquisition Officers (SLAOs). For displaced tribal landholders, market value determination applies rural multiplication factors along with 100% statutory solatium and 12% additional interest.

ALERT monitors land acquisition awards across Alluri Sitharama Raju and Eluru districts, ensuring displaced tribal families receive their complete statutory compensation under Schedule 1, rehabilitation entitlements under Schedule 2, and 25 basic community amenities in every resettlement colony under Schedule 3.

legal-compliances.title: Cases @ LA & RR Court (Legal Compliances)
legal-compliances.subtitle: Official RTI dataset of dispute petitions and compensation enhancement references filed before the Special LA & RR Authority Court (2017–2022).
paragraphs: The Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Authority (LA & RR Court) in Andhra Pradesh is established under Section 51 of the Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013 (RFCTLARR Act 2013). The Authority functions as a specialized civil court with exclusive statutory jurisdiction to determine disputes relating to land acquisition, compensation quantum, apportionment, and rehabilitation entitlements arising out of the Polavaram Irrigation Project.

Under Section 64 of the Act, project-displaced landholders and affected tribal families who have received compensation awards under protest may submit formal reference applications to the Land Acquisition Collector for transmission to the LA & RR Authority. The Authority adjudicates claims pertaining to undervaluation of agency agricultural lands, exclusion of non-notified submergence survey numbers, failure to award statutory solatium (100%) and interest, and denial of Second Schedule land-for-land resettlement entitlements.

Official RTI disclosures compiled from 2017 to 2022 document extensive case filings by displaced families across West Godavari and East Godavari agency tracts, including Polavaram, Buttayagudem, Devipatnam, Kunavaram, Chintoor, and VR Puram mandals. This legal compliance archive provides complete public access to the RTI documentation, case registry lists, dispute categories, and judicial remedies pursued by ALERT's legal cell to protect tribal rights.

An analysis of rejection orders reveals widespread statutory violations, including rejection without providing written reasons to Gram Sabhas, unlawful insistence on physical revenue documents over oral elder testimony, and arbitrary disqualification under Reserve Forest boundary claims.

rofr.title: Recognition of Forest Rights (RoFR) & Land Transfer Regulations (LTR)
rofr.subtitle: Securing ancestral tribal land rights under RoFR Act 2006 & AP Scheduled Areas LTR 1/70 across Andhra Pradesh.
paragraphs: The Scheduled Tribes and Other Traditional Forest Dwellers (Recognition of Forest Rights) Act, 2006 (RoFR Act) marks a historic turning point in recognizing the pre-existing customary rights of Adivasi and forest-dwelling communities over ancestral lands, community forest resources, and non-timber forest produce. ALERT actively mobilizes Gram Sabhas to map forest boundaries, verify traditional evidence, and secure both Individual Forest Rights (IFR) and Community Forest Resource (CFR) titles.

Complementing forest rights, the Andhra Pradesh Scheduled Areas Land Transfer Regulation 1 of 1970 (LTR 1/70) prohibits any transfer of immovable property in Scheduled Areas to non-tribals, presuming all land in Agency tracts belongs to Scheduled Tribes until proven otherwise. ALERT's legal cell monitors disposal trends, represents displaced Adivasis before appellate authorities, and provides field-level legal empowerment across Alluri Sitharama Raju (ASR) and Eluru districts.

flood-relief-measures.title: Flood Relief Measures - Emergency Disaster Response
flood-relief-measures.subtitle: Rapid response emergency relief, boat rescue operations, dry rations, and medical assistance across flooded Godavari agency tracts.
paragraphs: Every monsoon, the mighty Godavari overflows its banks, inundating dozens of habitations across Fifth-Scheduled agency mandals including Kunavaram, VR Puram, Chintoor, and Devipatnam. ALERT's emergency disaster response team deploys mechanized rescue boats, distributes dry ration hampers, establishes emergency medical camps, and provides waterproof tarpaulins to cut-off tribal families.

Over the last four years (2020–2023), ALERT has directly supported over 4,200+ Project Displaced Families and vulnerable Adivasi households, ensuring food security, child nutrition, and health support during devastating seasonal inundations.
